API Playground

A user tried Websets GitHub repo search for 'implementations of ReBAC authorization servers'. The preview returned things that were clearly not GitHub repos, and the matches lacked any mention of ReBAC. They estimated it was 'about 30/70 on finding the things I asked for… not worthless, but… AI does not solve all problems.'

The same user complained that the Websets results table fixes columns at 180px, truncating all descriptions and URLs. They also said the cURL in 'Get Code' was 'demonstrably wrong', with incorrect escaping that sends literal backslashes. Even the full search did not return only repos matching the criteria.

A user signed up for a trial account and was 'pretty impressed with the search API'. They were using it to integrate web-based docs into an employee-service agentic chatbot. Their one request was a cruft cleaner for results, to reduce what gets fed to the downstream LLM.

One user's first Websets search got one match and 14 misses. All other results stayed stuck on 'Verifying...' for minutes. They called it 'incomparably slower than Google; it's more like deep research.'
The site doesn't work at all with WebGL disabled. It just shows 'Application error: a client-side exception has occurred'. Another user said the hero globe is really laggy on a low-powered device.
A user searched for 'lucid air touring models available for sale Under 20,000 miles' and added a 'sale price' column. They could not get price details, and the same happened for other cars.
A user called the Exa LinkedIn webset 'very innovative'. They noted that many current data providers make it difficult, or against their ToS, to build products on their data.

A founder of a related startup (NewsCatcher) said 'I am a BIG Exa fan'. They agreed that SERP is not the right way for LLMs to interact with the web, and praised Websets' ability to sift through large numbers of pages.
An HN submission claims 'Exa.ai is indexing personal site data ignoring robots.txt'.

This feedback is on Metaphor, Exa's original search engine. A user tested the prompt 'My two favorite blogs are SlateStarCodex and' with the blog's newer name, AstralCodexTen. The top results were weird occult and esoteric blogs instead of rationalist blogs, suggesting it doesn't track renamed entities.

Also on Metaphor, Exa's original search engine: prompts like 'Here is an informative site about the 2020 election' returned election-fraud and misinformation sites as the single top result. Covid prompts returned similar results, e.g., fakepandemic.com.
